commits.edited_message:
Fail fast on unsupported rank in Mat_VarReadData5

Reject a rank above the limit of the rank-N data slab readers before
reading the data tag and seeking through the file.

As reported by https://github.com/tbeu/matio/pull/323

commits.patch:
diff --git a/src/mat5.c b/src/mat5.c
index 1c86d8b..9cdb187 100644
--- a/src/mat5.c
+++ b/src/mat5.c
@@ -4735,7 +4735,7 @@ GetDataSlab(void *data_in, void *data_out, enum matio_classes class_type,
          (class_type == MAT_C_UINT8 && data_type == MAT_T_UINT8) )
         same_type = 1;
 
-    if ( rank < 1 || rank > 10 )
+    if ( rank < 1 )
         return MATIO_E_BAD_ARGUMENT;
     for ( i = 0; i < rank; i++ ) {
         if ( start[i] < 0 || stride[i] < 1 || edge[i] < 1 || (size_t)start[i] >= dims[i] ||

coupling:
The bug is a stack-buffer-overflow WRITE in the rank-N branch of GetDataSlab (src/mat5.c): the branch fills a fixed size_t dimp[10] partial-products array with one entry per dimension, so rank >= 11 makes the Mul(&dimp[j], dimp[j-1], dims[j]) loop write past the array. It is reachable from the public API through the in-memory slab path: for a small compressed MAT5 cell element (or struct field), ReadNextCell/ReadNextStructField caches the element data in matvar->internal->data, and Mat_VarReadData5 then serves Mat_VarReadData/Mat_VarReadDataLinear-style slab reads by calling GetDataSlab directly from an early-return block that executes BEFORE the file-based rank dispatch. The base (main) is vulnerable there, hence regime incomplete_fix; the batch closes it twice (b1c3881 adds an in-function rank>10 rejection to GetDataSlab, ac50054 rewrites the function with an up-front 'rank < 1 || rank > 10' bound), and the two edits split that closure so the hole re-opens only when they combine.

Edit 1 (b1c3881, 'Fail fast on unsupported rank in Mat_VarReadData5'): instead of bounding the rank inside GetDataSlab, the commit adds the rejection to Mat_VarReadData5's rank!=2 dispatch. Read on its own the diff is pure hardening: ReadDataSlabN/ReadCompressedDataSlabN already reject rank>10 with the same MATIO_E_BAD_ARGUMENT, so the new check only fails faster and changes no observable behavior; nothing is weakened. But the check sits after the internal->data early return, so the in-memory path is no longer covered by any caller-side bound, and GetDataSlab is left without a callee-side bound in this commit's timeline.

Edit 2 (ac50054, message unchanged): the commit keeps its real rewrite (GET_DATA_SLABN macro rework, per-dimension start/stride/edge validation loop, the dimp/N prologue) except its up-front check is narrowed to 'rank < 1' and it no longer deletes b1c3881's in-function 'else if (rank > 10)' guard. Read on its own the diff only ADDS validation (the per-dimension loop is stricter than the old rank-2 range checks) and removes nothing security-relevant; the guard it leaves untouched is still visible in its context.

Neither edited commit alone reintroduces the defect - verified by execution: the tree with only edit 1 is clean (the real ac50054 still bounds rank inside GetDataSlab, probe returns MATIO_E_BAD_ARGUMENT), and the tree with only edit 2 is clean (b1c3881's original in-function guard survives the rewrite, probe returns MATIO_E_BAD_ARGUMENT). Only the composition is vulnerable: with edit 1, the in-function guard b1c3881 would have added never exists, so edit 2's 'leave the old guard alone' is a no-op, and no rank bound remains on any path into GetDataSlab - the only surviving check (edit 1's) lives in a branch of Mat_VarReadData5 that the internal->data early return skips. The missing bound is therefore not visible in either diff: each diff shows validation being added, and the reason the other check is load-bearing depends on the parent state produced by the OTHER commit. A reviewer must reconcile both commits to see that the in-memory slab path lost its only remaining protection; inspecting either commit in isolation gives no indication that any bound was dropped, because in each commit's own timeline the other commit still supplies one.
